title: Harrow: Synthesis of Optical Logic Circuits via Harmonic Mean and Integer Partition
problem: Photonic integrated circuits suffer from signal attenuation along light propagation paths, requiring optical-electrical conversions that introduce unwanted delays and inefficiency.
motivation: PICs offer energy-efficient computation over CMOS, but signal attenuation during optical logic synthesis limits practical implementations.
method: Harrow optimizes photonic logic synthesis from binary decision diagrams by improving the signal efficiency factor of optical combiners using harmonic mean optimization, and eliminates redundant combiners via integer partition. Techniques are arranged in an optimal operational sequence.
key_novelty: Harmonic mean-based optimization of DC combiners combined with integer partition redundancy elimination improves signal efficiency in optical logic synthesis.
contributions: Harmonic mean optimization of DC combiners to improve signal efficiency factor
Integer partition method to eliminate redundant optical combiners
Optimized operational sequence for combining techniques
Outperforms state-of-the-art in terms of efficiency factor
limitations: Specific efficiency metrics and performance numbers not disclosed in abstract; scalability to larger circuits not discussed.
